button.description: Buttons trigger actions and move people through a task. Choose a variant by priority and intent, not color alone.
button.choosingVariantIntro: Start with the action's priority in the current task, then choose the visual tone that matches its intent. Primary and Neutral are both high-emphasis actions; the difference is whether the action should carry the brand color.
button.primaryUseWhen: The main action in a task when brand emphasis is appropriate, such as Create project, Continue, or Publish.
button.primaryAvoid: Multiple Primary actions in the same region.
button.neutralUseWhen: The main action should remain neutral and independent of the brand color, such as Save, Confirm, or Sign in.
button.neutralAvoid: Placing it beside Primary as a competing main action.
button.destructiveUseWhen: An action is irreversible or high risk, such as Delete account or Remove member.
button.destructiveAvoid: Routine errors, cancel actions, or easily reversible changes.
button.secondaryUseWhen: A supporting alternative to the main action, such as Save draft, Preview, or Do this later.
button.secondaryAvoid: The only or most important call to action.
button.tertiaryUseWhen: A lower-priority standalone action still needs a visible boundary, such as Import or View details.
button.tertiaryAvoid: Crowded toolbars with many repeated controls.
button.ghostUseWhen: Toolbar, icon, or contextual actions already have enough surrounding structure.
button.ghostAvoid: The only call to action, or an action without enough surrounding context.
button.highEmphasisRule: Use one high-emphasis action per task region. Primary and Neutral are alternate expressions of the same priority; do not use them as competing actions.
button.compositionIntro: A button group should reveal the next step at a glance. Combine variants by priority, not by color or visual symmetry.
button.compositionRule1: Use one high-emphasis action in each task region.
button.compositionRule2: Choose either Primary or Neutral for that action; do not use both as peers.
button.compositionRule3: Pair the high-emphasis action with Secondary, Tertiary, or Ghost alternatives.
button.compositionRule4: Use Tertiary or Ghost for Cancel in most flows.
button.compositionRule5: Use Destructive as the high-emphasis action only when the dangerous choice is the current task.
button.label: Label
button.visualStyle: Controls the button's emphasis and visual tone. See Choosing a variant for usage guidance.
button.loadingDescription: Shows a spinner and disables the button.
button.activeDescription: Forces the pressed/held visual — e.g. while a dropdown or popover the button opened is showing.
button.asChildDescription: Merge props onto the child element instead of rendering a native button element.
